text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A organizes its argument into an introduction, multiple body paragraphs each with a distinct point (safety, economy), and a conclusion", "quality": "Structural organization", "description": "The essay develops its position across clearly delineated sections with topic sentences, whereas Essay B is a single undifferentiated block of text."}, {"evidence": "Essay A quotes the source article directly with quotation marks and paragraph citations, e.g., \"The information from the sensors can cause the car to apply brakes...\"(5)", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay integrates direct quotations from the article to support its claims, while Essay B offers no cited evidence from the source."}, {"evidence": "Essay A develops multiple supporting reasons including driver safety assistance and economic benefits", "quality": "Development of reasoning", "description": "The essay elaborates each supporting point with explanation and connection to the source, whereas Essay B merely asserts dangers without developing them."}, {"evidence": "Essay A acknowledges counterpoints, noting the cars are 'not 100% capable' and that there are 'some things that are not too particularly great'", "quality": "Balance and acknowledgment of opposing views", "description": "The essay concedes limitations of driverless cars while still defending its position, giving the argument more nuance than Essay B's one-sided treatment."}, {"evidence": "Essay A uses varied sentence structures and transitions such as 'However,' 'Essentially,' 'Not only to mention,' and 'In conclusion'", "quality": "Sentence fluency and cohesion", "description": "The essay connects ideas with transitional language and varied syntax, while Essay B relies on run-on sentences and repetitive phrasing."}]}
